hotkey._comment: Dictation key. 'key' is Windows/Linux (Right Ctrl), 'key_mac' is macOS (Right Command). scan_code is a Windows-only exact override: run `run.bat probe`, press your key, and put the code it prints here with 'key' set to null.

hotkey_ask._comment: Hold this key and speak to ask instead of dictating; the answer is printed, shown, and spoken, never pasted. With memory on, every question searches your connected sources first and falls back to the plain assistant when nothing matches; say the trigger phrase to ask memory only. Standalone key: 'right alt' on Windows/Linux, 'right option' on macOS (dictation is Right Command there, so Right Option is free). scan_code is a Windows-only exact override, same as the dictation block - use `run.bat probe` if Right Alt does not fire. Alternatively leave 'key' null and set 'modifier' to chord onto the dictation key.

tts._comment: Reads answers aloud. Needs `install.py --tts` once: it adds kokoro-onnx and downloads the 82M model. Engine is 'kokoro' for now.

memory._comment2: rerank_model names a folder under models/. ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 (23M) scores ~35 ms per candidate on the reference CPU; bge-reranker-v2-m3 (568M, multilingual) is ~500 ms and made a lookup take 12 s, so it is opt-in. rerank_pool is how many fused candidates the cross-encoder scores - the single biggest cost in a request.
memory._comment: The local context engine. Needs `install.py --memory` once. Say 'hey jar, ...' mid-dictation to compose an answer from your connected sources at the cursor; the ask key searches those sources on every question and speaks the answer, no trigger needed. The trigger is matched ignoring spaces, so 'heyjar' works too. open_ui brings up the connector window with the keyboard; `run.bat --no-ui` skips it for one run.

hosted_fallback._comment: Compose and ask only - never dictation cleanup, never fact extraction. Put OPENAI_API_KEY in .env (see .env.example). mode 'always' sends every lookup; 'fallback' keeps the local 3B in front and only pays the network when it comes back empty. Any OpenAI-shaped endpoint works via base_url. max_tokens must also cover reasoning tokens, which are billed and counted but never shown - too low and the reply comes back empty. Measured on the real mailbox: hosted 9/9 correct with 0 hallucinations vs local 8/9 with 1, and 3.7s vs 12s. Run `python -m memory.answer_eval [--local]` to re-measure after any change.

compose._comment: The paste-at-cursor half of memory. tier 'auto' picks by hardware; model overrides it explicitly (null reuses the warm cleanup model - correct on 4 GB GPUs). hosted_fallback applies to compose only, never extraction, and stays off unless you turn it on. timeout_sec covers the whole retrieved-context call: eight mail chunks is a ~3000-token prefill, which at 30s was timing out under memory pressure and being reported as 'nothing found'.
